Thank you all for flagging these constraints. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I propose a sequence:

1. Jon: Furnace 7's thermocouple calibration certificate expires before this production window. A 2-hour recalibration is required before we can go into production.
2. Priya: Batch Q requires 15 first-piece hardness tests completed and held for review before release, per a revised control plan not yet on the traveler.
3. Carlos: Batch R's staged alloy charge will oxidize if it sits at the furnace bay for more than 4 hours, so R must run first.
4. Elena: The installed gas analyzer failed its bump test and must be replaced with the spare before any run can proceed.

So we have two pre-production tasks — the 2-hour thermocouple recalibration and the gas analyzer replacement — both of which need to be completed before we start any batch. And R must be first due to the oxidation constraint.

Proposed sequence: R first, then Q, then P.

R runs first to stay within the 4-hour oxidation window. Q second so we can get the 15 first-piece hardness tests underway and in review while P is being prepared. P last.

Can I get sign-off from each of you on this sequence and the associated constraints? Jon, can you confirm the recalibration will be done before startup? Elena, can you confirm the spare gas analyzer will be installed before startup? Priya, can you confirm the 15-test requirement will be noted on the traveler? Carlos, can you confirm R first works for the oxidation constraint?
